title: SDK incremental tutorials & fail-fast labs playbook
body:
Context:
Quick, sink-or-swim mini-lessons for new devs integrating Redwood SDKs into product flows. Focus: 5--15 minute guided exercises that surface the most common failure modes (auth, timeouts, streaming), teach cost-aware patterns (batching, cache keys), and include a deterministic failure-injection step so engineers can observe fallback behavior locally.

Audience:
- Product engineers adding a single endpoint to a webapp
- Platform integrators testing local failovers
- Solutions engineers running customer demos

Design principles (short):
- Start small: one API call + one observable metric
- Local-first: reproduce network latency and kv-cache hits in the dev loop
- Fail-fast: each lab ends with an intentional fault to exercise fallbacks
- Measurable: each tutorial includes a telemetry assertion and a token/cost estimate

Micro-tutorials (proposed sequence):
1) hello-gen: wire a text-generation request, display streaming tokens, assert 200 and <250ms baseline
2) auth-toggle: swap api keys (valid -> revoked) to show error shapes and recommended errors-to-copy for UX
3) batching-lite: compare single vs batched calls, log token delta and throughput effect
4) prefix-cache: enable simple KV-prefetch, show cache-hit/miss counters and how to warm prefixes
5) fallback-matrix: configure routing policy (latency -> cost) and simulate capacity shortage to trigger variant fallback
6) abrupt-reconnect: simulate socket/region blip to test automatic retry and idempotency notes
7) prompt-regression-smoke: run golden prompt set, capture embeddings + outputs, show diff and alert conditions

Failure-injection experiments:
- local-proxy (netem-like) script included to add jitter/packet-loss
- env var REDWOOD_FORCE_FALLBACK to force variant selection path
- sample harness emits gcpm-like traces so console can show spans

Telemetry & gating:
- Each lab writes a small JSON "lab-result" to ./results with fields: outcome, latency_ms, tokens_used, telemetry_hash (simple sha1 of inputs)
- CI job (sdk/labs/quickchecks) replays the labs against the latest SDK and fails on: unexpected error kinds, token delta > 15% vs baseline, missing span IDs

Acceptance criteria for release to docs-site:
- Every tutorial has: README, runnable Docker dev image, one-liner start script, and a 3-step checklist for success/failure observations
- Two sample apps (node + python) showing identical flow and the same telemetry assertions
- Playbook includes troubleshooting table with top 8 failure fingerprints and mitigation steps

Next steps / short backlog:
- Draft README templates (owner: Samir)
- Build netem wrapper and Dockerfile (owner: Marina)
- Add CI replay job and result uploader (owner: Elena)
- UX copy for error messages and developer-facing hints (owner: Developer Docs)

Open questions / TODO:
- Do we include a long-running expensive token estimate for each lab or keep all labs tiny? (tradeoff: demo realism vs cloud cost)
- Where should the canonical lab result artifacts live (Drive vs S3 vs Confluence)? Prefer S3 but need cross-team access plan
- Add a short video walkthrough (60--90s) for each lab? High impact but extra production work

Notes to self: keep labs focused on observable wins (latency reduction, cost per 1k tokens, fallback correctness). Avoid duplicating larger onramp guides — these should plug into existing quickstarts but be deliberately lower friction and more testable.
